t: You are at Gilbert House, a mid-rise terrace block of the Barbican Estate. It takes its name from Sir Humphrey Gilbert, an Elizabethan adventurer, explorer, member of parliament and soldier, who served under Queen Elizabeth the First. He was a pioneer of the English colonial empire in North America and of the plantations of Ireland. Gilbert was also a half-brother of Sir Walter Raleigh, and a cousin of Sir Richard Grenville. Like other blocks on the estate, the name looks back to figures of the Tudor age.
